column6: old text (not edited): Q4 explanation uses "crucial", Explainer and Q4 answer use "essential"; Q5 explanation conflates threshold signatures with multi-sig wallets.
Bullet 2 said chunking "gives no threshold"; plain chunking is an n-of-n split, so changed to "needs every piece to rebuild the key".
old text (not edited): Explainer says the ideal/real definition captures fairness; fairness cannot be had in general without an honest majority (Cleve 1986).

Bullet 4 dropped qualifiers (general functions, no trusted setup; correlated randomness allows IT security with dishonest majority) and called oblivious transfer an assumption; reworded so OT is built from computational assumptions.

old text (not edited): Q5 explanation says Deep Crack broke DES "in 22 hours in 1998"; Deep Crack took 56 hours in July 1998, and 22 hours 15 minutes was the January 1999 Deep Crack plus distributed.net run. Q3 "2^128!" should read (2^128)!.

New bullet 2 is correct but contradicts old Core Idea text "cryptocurrency custody (multi-sig wallets)"; the Core Idea conflates threshold signatures with multisig and should be reworded (not edited, old text).
old text (not edited): Explainer says PCPs let "exponentially long proofs" be verified by sampling; PCPs for NP are polynomial length.

old text (not edited, clearly wrong): Core Idea says arguments allow "polynomial-time provers to cheat"; it is the reverse (sound against poly-time provers, unbounded can cheat). Q1 answer says statistical soundness "requires multiple rounds"; statistically sound NIZK proofs exist in the CRS model. Q3 is a true-false item phrased as a "what is the difference" question. Explainer uses "journey" and says STARKs are "post-quantum secure" (plausibly).
Bullet 1 overstated: "Transparent schemes ... still rest on idealized hash functions"; some transparent NIZKs use a uniform random string in the standard model. Added "Practical" and "usually".
Bullet 1 stated "Soundness is probabilistic" as an absolute; perfectly sound NIZK proofs exist (e.g. Groth-Ostrovsky-Sahai). Added "usually".
